title: setRewardToken mid-life leaves stale tokenConfig assumptions
justification: Spec deviation with value-leak path: switching reward token changes the denormalization base and tokenConfig assumptions. Front-running a pending claim with setRewardToken can DoS the claim or shift the payment unit silently. Stated assumption: owner action; architectural gap is the missing two-step migration / claim-time expectedRewardToken parameter. Medium because the claimer can be forced into a different payment asset than simulated.
preconditions: Owner calls setRewardToken between claimer simulation and inclusion (legitimate or malicious).
impact: Claim DoS or silent payment-unit substitution; claimer pays in unexpected token at unexpected rate.
attack_path_summary: 1) Bot simulates claim with rewardToken=USDC, sets slippage. 2) Owner front-runs with setRewardToken(DAI). 3) Claim either reverts (no allowance / no config) or pays in DAI at altered terms.
